A.note: Strongest is the discipline of measuring every interval itself from consecutive `tst` rather than assuming cadence; weakest is the PERCENTILE_CONT analytic used inside a windowed GROUP BY, which the answer itself doubts and which would not run.

B.note: Strongest is the peer residual that separates a sick vehicle from a sick corridor; weakest is cadence_ratio, whose count-over-covered-seconds arithmetic reads as a completeness score and is easy to misinterpret.

C.note: Strongest is the explicitly grounded refusal set and the units-aware choice of `odo` over coordinate geometry; weakest is the WITHIN GROUP spelling of PERCENTILE_CONT, which is not this dialect's syntax.

D.note: Strongest is the careful identification of the last record carrying a `stop` as the departure proxy; weakest is discarding `dl` and averaging `occu`, which leaves the two headline metrics resting on unit guesses, plus COUNT(DISTINCT) and LAG over an aggregate that likely will not run.

blinding.why: C names the most specific machine-readable detail — semanticRole, phenomenonTimeRelation, supportPeriod, coordinateReferenceSystem with axis order, and metre units — while D repeatedly asserts that units and cadence are undeclared.
